In the bath after janaba the Prophet washed his hands, made ablution and poured water over himself; he shared one pot with a wife, and a sa' sufficed.
The Prophet poured water thrice on his head, rubbed scent into it, washed his private parts, cleaned his hand with earth, washed his feet last and declined a towel.
The Prophet and a wife bathed from one pot in turn; he washed his hands first, and Maimuna, who screened him, described each step and how he declined a towel.
The Prophet's janaba bath began with ablution and ended with the feet; once he recalled janaba at the iqama and went to bathe, and women pour thrice on the head.
Fatima and Maimuna screened the Prophet while he bathed, and he told Um Sulaim a woman must bathe after a wet dream if she sees discharge.
A junub person may sleep after washing his private parts and making ablution, as the Prophet did and told Umar.
Intercourse makes the bath compulsory; Uthman and others reported washing and ablution when there is no emission, but the bath is called safer and the final ruling.
